correctness.rationale: For 0<θ<π/2 and independent area-uniform points on |z|≤sinθ⊂S², the two-point spherical Blaschke–Petkantschin formula disintegrates pairs by unoriented great circles with density |sin(u−v)|. A circle of inclination i≤θ is entirely in the band; for i>θ it meets the zone in two antipodal arcs of length L=2arcsin(sinθ/sin i)<π. Exactly opposite-component endpoint pairs have a minimizing geodesic escaping. The weighted opposite-pair integral equals 4(L−sin L), reducing escape probability to I(s)/(2πs²). Differentiation of I(s) gives I′(s)=2πs−πs/sqrt(1−s²), hence I(s)=πsqrt(1−s²)(1−sqrt(1−s²)) from I(0)=0. Thus P=cosθ/(2(1+cosθ)), strictly decreasing to 0 as θ→π/2, and tending to 1/4 as θ↓0, while exactly-on-equator sampling gives 0. Independent high-precision quadrature at five θ confirms normalization; it is not used as proof.
